name: EvolveR: Self-Evolving LLM Agents through an Experience-Driven Lifecycle
venue: Accepted by ICML 2026 (per arXiv comment and official repo, paper accepted at ICML 2026, ~2026-05-01). Preprint arXiv:2510.16079 (cs.CL / cs.AI), submitted 17 Oct 2025 (v1), last revised 16 May 2026 (v3).

Model weights: https://huggingface.co/Edaizi/EvolveR (EvolveR-3B); data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Edaizi/EvolveR-NQ-HotpotQA.
task_domain: QA / agentic decision-making: knowledge-intensive open-domain and multi-hop question answering with tool use (search engine), framed as an LLM-agent self-evolution problem. Primary focus is multi-hop QA; method is positioned as a general experience-driven lifecycle paradigm.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent, closed-loop self-evolving agent with parameter updates. The agent operates in a Think-Act-Observe loop over an action space of {<search_experience>, <search_knowledge>, <answer>}. The lifecycle alternates two phases that share the same trajectories: (1) Offline Self-Distillation, where the policy parameters are FROZEN and the agent's own model distills its past success/failure trajectories into abstract reusable strategic 'principles' that are curated into an Experience Base E (with semantic dedup, merge/integration, dynamic utility scoring, and pruning); (2) Online Interaction, where the agent solves tasks, actively retrieves distilled principles to guide reasoning, and accumulates new behavioral trajectories. The loop is closed by a Policy Evolution mechanism that uses GRPO reinforcement learning on the online trajectories (composite outcome + format reward) to update the policy. Supervision: ground-truth answers provide a sparse binary outcome (Exact Match) reward; a dense format/shaping reward encourages balanced reasoning and search. A cold-start SFT stage (~700 NQ+HotpotQA samples, LoRA, trajectories from GPT-4o) teaches the interaction format before RL. In-domain training data (NQ, HotpotQA train splits) builds the experience base; out-of-domain datasets are used only for evaluating generalization. Trained on 8x A100 (80GB) GPUs; full 3B lifecycle ~39.4 hours.
what_is_retrieved: Two distinct retrieval targets during online interaction: (1) distilled strategic PRINCIPLES (guiding principles from successes, cautionary principles from failures) from the agent's own internal Experience Base E (these are the self-learned experiences central to the method); and (2) factual DOCUMENTS from an external knowledge base / search engine (Wikipedia corpus) via <search_knowledge>. The experience principles (abstracted guidelines/rules paired with structured knowledge triples) are the novel retrieval unit; documents are standard RAG-style factual retrieval.
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID. The agent retrieves from (a) a GROWING/episodic internal Experience Base E that the agent writes itself (self-distilled principles, grown during training across the closed loop), and (b) a STATIC external knowledge corpus (Wikipedia, via a search engine / dense retriever) for factual grounding. The defining novelty (experience principles) targets a self-written, evolving memory; the knowledge search targets a fixed external corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking objective for both retrieval streams: <search_experience> returns top-k_e = 3 principles from E; <search_knowledge> returns top-k_d = 3 documents. No completeness / minimal-set objective and no precision-driven variable-size recommendation; selection is fixed top-3 nearest-neighbor by embedding similarity. (The agent may issue multiple search calls per episode, but each call is fixed-top-3.)
retrieval_unit: guideline-rule / principle (problem-solving strategic principle): each retrieved experience unit is a distilled abstract principle = a one-sentence natural-language description plus several structured (subject, predicate, object) knowledge triples, tagged as guiding (from success) or cautionary (from failure), and carrying a metric score and usage/success counts. The complementary knowledge-search unit is a document (Wikipedia passage). So the primary novel unit is a distilled strategic guideline-rule; the secondary unit is a document.
index_source: Hybrid. The Experience Base E is a GROWING memory induced online/across the closed training loop from the agent's own trajectories (offline self-distillation phases interleaved with online interaction); principles are added/merged/pruned over time (grows to ~50k principles during training). The external knowledge index is a STATIC pre-built corpus (Wikipedia-18 corpus with e5 embeddings, served via a local FAISS/Pyserini retrieval server, following Search-R1).
index_structure_topology: Experience Base: flat vector index of principle embeddings (BGE-M3 embeddings) for cosine-similarity nearest-neighbor search, implemented with Milvus (paper) / a vector DB; each principle additionally carries metadata (metric score, usage/success counts) and structured knowledge triples, and is linked to its source trajectories via the Merge operation (a loose, per-principle trajectory-linking structure rather than a global graph). External knowledge base: flat dense vector index (e5 embeddings over Wikipedia, FAISS Flat index). Overall: flat vector indices with metadata/score keying; not a hierarchical or global knowledge graph (though principles embed local triples).
retriever_type: Dense (embedding-based) nearest-neighbor retriever for both streams. Experience retrieval uses BGE-M3 embeddings with cosine similarity (Milvus); knowledge retrieval uses dense e5 embeddings over Wikipedia (FAISS), following Search-R1. Off-the-shelf embedders (not a learned retriever); however, the agent's policy that DECIDES when/what to query is RL-trained (GRPO), so query issuance is a learned policy while the similarity matching itself is fixed dense ANN.
retriever_learning_signal: The embedding-based matching is off-the-shelf (no contrastive fine-tuning of BGE-M3 or e5). However, the decision of WHEN and WHAT to retrieve is learned: the agent's policy is trained via GRPO reinforcement learning with a composite reward (sparse outcome EM reward + dense format reward that explicitly rewards using <search_experience> and <search_knowledge> diversity and balanced reasoning steps). Thus the retrieval-action policy is RL/task-effectiveness-optimized, while the underlying similarity retriever is fixed similarity. Additionally, principle selection over time is shaped by a utility-based dynamic metric score s(p) = (c_succ+1)/(c_use+2) that prunes low-utility principles (utility/effectiveness signal on the store, not on the embedder).
query_construction: Agent-generated, thought-conditioned queries. Inside its <think> reasoning, the agent issues a <search_experience> query (often expressed as candidate principle triples / intent it is looking for) to fetch relevant principles, and/or a <search_knowledge> query (a natural-language search query) for facts. Queries are free-form natural-language strings produced by the policy mid-reasoning, conditioned on the current state/question; not raw-input-only and not fixed templates.
query_granularity: step/state-level (within-episode, two-stream): the agent can issue retrieval queries at any point in its multi-turn Think-Act-Observe loop, conditioned on its current reasoning state, and can search multiple times per episode (converging to ~2 experience searches and ~4 knowledge searches per trajectory). Not a single one-shot task-level retrieval; retrieval is interleaved per reasoning step / per tool-call.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative / agent-initiated (adaptive within the loop): retrieval is triggered by the agent's own decision to emit a <search_experience> or <search_knowledge> action during reasoning, and can occur multiple times per episode. The learned policy (RL-shaped) governs the timing; there is no fixed schedule, no token-confidence trigger.
retrieval_trigger_signal: agent-initiated request: the agent autonomously decides to issue <search_experience> / <search_knowledge> actions from within its <think> reasoning. The format reward shapes this behavior (rewarding diverse and sufficient search use), so the trigger is a learned, policy-driven action rather than an external confidence/uncertainty/attention signal or a learned complexity classifier.
reranking: None. Both experience and knowledge retrieval return the top-3 by embedding similarity directly with no separate cross-encoder, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranking stage. (Principle ordering/prioritization is influenced over time by the dynamic metric score, but there is no per-query reranking module described.)
retrieved_context_refinement: Minimal at retrieval time for the online phase: retrieved principles (with their scores and triples) and retrieved documents are injected into context as observations (<experience>...</experience> and <information>...</information>) and consumed by the agent's reasoning; they are loss-masked during the policy update. The heavy refinement happens at WRITE time on the experience store (distillation into abstract principles, semantic deduplication, merge/integration, utility scoring, and pruning), not as post-retrieval document distillation/compression at query time. So online: none/light; offline curation: distill + dedup + filter.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation + training signal. (1) Prompt augmentation: retrieved principles provide heuristic strategic guidance that shapes the agent's <think> monologue and steers subsequent <search_knowledge> actions; retrieved documents provide factual grounding. (2) Training signal: because online trajectories are conditioned on retrieved principles, the GRPO update learns a policy of how to effectively utilize the agent's own distilled wisdom (reinforcing the link between retrieving high-quality principles and producing high-reward outcomes). Retrieved-token loss is masked (not directly absorbed into parameters); an exp-absorb ablation that unmasked principle tokens slightly hurt performance.
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved within an agentic reasoning/acting loop (retrieve-while-think). The agent runs a multi-turn Think-Act-Observe loop and weaves principle retrieval and knowledge retrieval into its reasoning at chosen steps, then answers. Plans are not produced one-shot; principles act as retrieve-then-reason heuristic guidance that influences the agent's next actions inside the loop. No explicit MCTS/tree search; integration is inside an interleaved search-and-reason loop optimized by RL.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-CoT-step / per-tool-call within a rollout: retrieval (experience and knowledge) is interleaved at the granularity of individual reasoning steps and tool-calls within a single episode (multiple <think>, <search_experience>, <search_knowledge> actions per trajectory before the final <answer>).
retrieved_item_representation: Distilled strategy/guideline (free-text rule) paired with structured knowledge triples: each principle is injected as a natural-language description plus (subject, predicate, object) triplets, tagged guiding/cautionary, and annotated with its metric score (e.g. 'type: guiding, metric score: 0.67, description: ...'). Knowledge results are injected as raw document passages. The novel surface form is the distilled strategic principle (structured note + triples), not a raw trajectory or executable program.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled strategy/insight, specifically state-aware strategic guidelines/rules (e.g. 'For comparison questions, gather data on both items before concluding'; 'When determining character relationships in a series, avoid assuming actors based solely on character recognition; confirm with verified role descriptions'). Explicitly NOT raw trajectories - the paper contrasts itself with 'learning by raw trajectories' and emphasizes abstraction into reusable principles. The complementary knowledge units are raw documents (low abstraction).
noise_robustness_mechanism: Multiple: (1) utility-based DYNAMIC SCORING and PRUNING - each principle's metric score s(p)=(c_succ+1)/(c_use+2) tracks historical effectiveness; principles below threshold theta_prune=0.3 are periodically pruned (manual annotation shows this cuts incorrect/misleading principles from 24% to 8% and raises 'ideal' principles from 26% to 82%). (2) Semantic DEDUPLICATION + a two-stage matching/merge (embedding pre-filter at theta_sim=0.85 then LLM binary equivalence judgment) keeps E compact and avoids redundant/noisy entries. (3) RL-conditioned policy learns to selectively use helpful principles. (4) Retrieved tokens are loss-masked (an exp-absorb variant that unmasks them degraded performance, attributed to noisy/irrelevant top-k principles). Scalability test to ~50k principles shows stable, non-collapsing performance, evidencing robustness to long-term noise.
memory_type: Procedural / strategic experience memory: an Experience Base E of distilled abstract problem-solving principles (guiding + cautionary) with structured triples and utility scores. It is derived from episodic trajectories but stored as abstracted procedural/strategic knowledge rather than raw episodes. Plus an external static factual knowledge store (not a learned/grown memory).
write_back: Yes. The offline self-distillation phase writes newly distilled principles into E (add as new entry if novel, else Merge the new trajectory under the most similar existing principle). It also updates per-principle usage/success counts and metric scores, and prunes low-utility principles. So the system actively stores, merges, scores, and removes experiences.
online_growth: Yes, the Experience Base grows across the closed-loop training process (interleaved online interaction + offline distillation), expanding from ~4k to ~50k principles during training (with dedup/pruning keeping it compact and curated). The growth is driven by the lifecycle loop during training; at fixed evaluation time the trained policy retrieves from the curated base. (Growth is across training iterations rather than a streaming test-time-only deployment, but it is genuinely online within the lifecycle, not a frozen offline-only induction.)
write_back_trigger: On-success-and-failure, reflective (during the offline self-distillation phase). After collecting trajectories online, the agent reviews each trajectory by outcome: successful trajectories yield a guiding principle, failed trajectories yield a cautionary principle (Exact-Match correctness determines outcome). New principles trigger dedup/merge writes; usage/success counts update when principles are used; low-score principles trigger pruning sweeps. Writes occur in the offline reflection phase, not per-step during the answer-producing rollout.
failure_experience_usage: Success + failure, used contrastively/correctively. Successful trajectories distill into GUIDING principles; FAILED trajectories distill into CAUTIONARY principles (explicit 'what to avoid' rules with failure-pattern triples). Both kinds are stored in E and retrievable. Additionally, the RL/GRPO update itself leverages both positive and negative rollouts (learn what to do from successes, what to avoid from failures), which the paper argues is why GRPO beats SFT-on-successes-only (0.382 vs 0.357 on 3B).
memory_evolution_update: Link-and-evolve with dedup-merge and forget-prune: new principles are deduplicated (semantic pre-filter + LLM equivalence) and either added or Merged under an existing principle (linking the new source trajectory and strengthening it with new evidence); each principle's metric score and usage/success counts are continuously updated; principles whose score falls below theta_prune=0.3 are periodically pruned (forget). Longitudinal analysis shows later-created principles have higher average metric scores (0.462 -> 0.500), indicating the store and the distillation ability co-evolve. Not append-only.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partially. The similarity matching (BGE-M3 / e5 cosine top-k) is a fixed non-learned retriever, but the DECISION to retrieve and WHAT to query (issuing <search_experience>/<search_knowledge> with policy-generated queries) is an RL-LEARNED policy (GRPO with a reward that explicitly incentivizes effective experience/knowledge search), and principle prioritization in the store is governed by a learned utility score. So case-selection/use is partly a learned policy layered on fixed similarity retrieval, not pure fixed top-k.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private memory: one EvolveR agent distills, curates, retrieves, and learns from its own Experience Base. No sharing across multiple agents or heterogeneous frameworks (the paper notes inspiration from multi-agent memory frameworks like G-Memory but does not implement cross-agent experience sharing).
benchmarks: Seven QA benchmarks. In-domain (train splits used to build the experience base): Natural Questions (NQ) and HotpotQA (multi-hop). Out-of-domain (generalization only): TriviaQA, PopQA (general QA), and 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue, Bamboogle (multi-hop). External retrieval over a Wikipedia-18 corpus. Models: Qwen2.5 family (0.5B, 1.5B, 3B, 7B).
benchmark_family: QA / multi-hop QA (open-domain single-hop: NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA; multi-hop: HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue, Bamboogle). No web/embodied/tool/code/memory/decision-RL benchmark families.
baselines: Three paradigms, all on Qwen2.5 base models: (1) Prompting-based (no parameter updates): Direct Inference, Chain-of-Thought (CoT), RAG, IRCoT, Search-o1. (2) SFT-based: standard SFT, Rejection Sampling. (3) RL-based (direct competitors): Search-R1 (base and instruct variants; with search engine), DeepSeek-R1-style R1-base / R1-instruct (reasoning without search). The closest competitor is Search-R1.
key_metrics: Primary: Exact Match (EM) after standard normalization (main results). Secondary: F1 Score (reported in the model-scale generalizability analysis). Auxiliary diagnostics: average action counts per trajectory (<think>, <search_knowledge>, <search_experience>), top-3 retrieval search latency (seconds), experience-base size (number of principles), and principle quality annotation percentages.
headline_result: On the QA benchmark suite, EvolveR achieves the best average EM, outperforming all baselines including the strong RL agent Search-R1: average EM 0.382 on Qwen2.5-3B (vs 0.325 for Search-R1-instruct) and 0.417 on Qwen2.5-7B (vs 0.385 for Search-R1-instruct). It secures best scores on in-domain NQ (0.434/0.462 at 3B/7B), out-of-domain PopQA, and the adversarial Bamboogle, while staying competitive elsewhere.
ablations: (1) Self- vs teacher-distillation (Table 2): scale-dependent reversal - GPT-4o-mini teacher distillation helps small models (0.5B: 0.220 teacher vs 0.150 self), but at 3B self-distill (0.382) BEATS teacher-distill (0.370), validating 'cognitive alignment'. (2) Experience retrieval at inference (Table 3): disabling exp-retrieve (same trained model) drops 3B avg from 0.382 -> 0.340 (and far more on smaller models, e.g. 0.150 -> 0.078 at 0.5B), showing retrieval is indispensable. (3) Component attribution (Table 4, 3B): none 0.134; RL-only 0.325; distill+retrieve no-RL 0.357; distill+RL no-retrieve 0.340; full (distill+retrieve+RL) 0.382 - retrieval and RL are complementary. (4) Memory configuration (Table 5): no-base 0.325 < teacher-distilled 0.370 < self-distilled 0.382. (5) RL vs SFT on the same successful trajectories (Table 8): GRPO 0.382 > SFT 0.357 (~7% relative), because RL uses both successes and failures. (6) Pruning-threshold sensitivity (Table 9): robust across theta_prune in {0.1,0.3,0.7,0.9} (avg ~0.265-0.276 at 1.5B). (7) Experience internalization (Table 11): unmasking principle tokens (exp-absorb) slightly hurts (0.382 -> 0.371). (8) Principle-quality annotation (Table 6) and scalability to ~50k principles (Table 7) confirm scoring/pruning efficacy and stability.
evaluation_decoupling: Partial. The end-to-end task metric (EM, plus F1) is the primary report. Intrinsic retrieval-ranking metrics (Recall@k / nDCG) are NOT reported. However, intrinsic experience-store quality IS reported separately via manual principle-quality annotation (Ideal/Vague/Incorrect % by score tier) and principle-quality-by-creation-phase metric scores, plus retrieval latency vs accuracy as the base scales - so experience-curation quality is decoupled, but classic retrieval IR metrics are not.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mostly outcome (EM/F1), but with notable process-level analysis: longitudinal tracking of action frequencies (<think>/<search_knowledge>/<search_experience> per trajectory across training, converging to ~6 reasoning / ~4 knowledge / ~2 experience), principle-quality annotation (process artifact quality), principle metric-score evolution over training intervals, and a qualitative rollout case study. No formal step-wise reasoning-faithfulness score.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported. Training cost: full Qwen2.5-3B lifecycle (cold-start SFT + GRPO RL) ~39.4 hours on 8x A100 (80GB). Experience-retrieval latency (Milvus): ~0.06s for top-3 over ~14k principles, scaling to only ~0.20s at ~50k principles - negligible vs LLM generation. RL rollout: G=8 trajectories per prompt, batch 128 prompts; vLLM-accelerated. Accuracy stays stable/peaks (avg EM up to 0.410 at 45k) as the base grows, showing favorable scalability/cost vs accuracy. Knowledge retrieval is top-3 docs per call; the agent converges to ~4 knowledge + ~2 experience searches per trajectory.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k, budget-capped. Per <search_knowledge> action: top-k_d=3 documents; per <search_experience> action: top-k_e=3 principles. Max input sequence length 8192 tokens, max response 1024 tokens. The agent may issue multiple searches per episode (no fixed total cap; format reward gives a diversity score and a quantity bonus up to 6 searches). Cold-start uses ~700 SFT samples. Selection is fixed top-3 retrieved-then-used (not adaptive/precision-driven k).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing QA benchmarks: NQ, HotpotQA, TriviaQA, PopQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue, Bamboogle; external Wikipedia-18 corpus; follows Search-R1 / O2-Searcher data setup). Does not construct a new benchmark.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes (embedding top-3 retrieval of principles from E via <search_experience>), Reuse: yes (principles applied as heuristic guidance in the agent's reasoning, plus RL reinforces effective reuse), Revise: partial/yes (principles are merged/integrated and their utility scores updated, and the self-distillation ability improves over time; but a retrieved principle is used as-is as guidance rather than per-instance adapted), Retain: yes (distill new principles, dedup/merge, score, prune into E)]. All four CBR phases are present in spirit, with Reuse mediated by an RL-trained policy.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself as an 'experience-driven self-evolution lifecycle' / self-evolving agents / experiential learning and continual learning; it does NOT cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner and does not use the term 'case-based reasoning'. It realizes CBR-like Retrieve/Reuse/Retain mechanisms (with abstraction into principles) under a self-evolution + RL framing.
tool_document_engineering: N/A for tool retrieval. The experience-principle 'documents' are engineered, though: trajectories are distilled by the agent's own policy into a structured principle = NL description + (subject,predicate,object) triples, with semantic deduplication, merge/integration, and a dynamic utility metric_score, before being embedded (BGE-M3) and indexed. This is principle/experience engineering rather than tool-docstring engineering.
index_content_separation: Partial. Each principle stores a compact description + triples + score as the retrievable/indexed unit, with the merge step LINKING source trajectories to a principle (heavier raw trajectory content is associated but the lightweight principle is what is retrieved and injected). This is a light-index-then-(optionally)-associated-content pattern, though the paper does not emphasize progressive disclosure.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A as a tool store. The external knowledge tool is a fixed local Wikipedia search engine (FAISS/Pyserini retrieval server, following Search-R1), not an MCP/RapidAPI/RESTful live tool index. The internal Experience Base is a dynamically updated vector DB (Milvus) of self-distilled principles with CRUD-like add/merge/prune operations, but it stores experiences, not external tool APIs.
adaptation_mechanism: Primarily LLM-prompted/policy-guided reuse rather than per-case solution rewriting: a retrieved principle is applied verbatim as heuristic guidance that conditions the agent's reasoning and subsequent actions, and the RL-trained policy learns to apply principles effectively (RL-reuse-finetuning). Adaptation/revision happens at the store level (offline self-distillation revises and merges principles, utility scoring prunes weak ones) rather than rewriting a retrieved case at solve time.
builds_on: Search-R1 (Jin et al. 2025; RL-trained search agent, interaction format, retrieval setup, ~700-sample cold-start, top-3 doc retrieval) and O2-Searcher (Mei et al. 2025; same group, search-based agent) as the agentic-RL backbone; GRPO from DeepSeekMath (Shao et al. 2024) and DeepSeek-R1 (Guo et al. 2025; cold-start + RL recipe) for policy optimization; ReAct (Yao et al. 2023) Think-Act-Observe loop and Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023) for the experiential/self-reflection lineage; ExpeL (Zhao et al. 2024) and Memento (Zhou et al. 2025) as prior experience/reflection-memory agents; structured-memory frameworks Mem0 (Chhikara et al. 2025) and G-Memory (Zhang et al. 2025) for the description+triples principle representation; BGE-M3 embeddings; verl RL framework; LLaMA-Factory + LoRA; vLLM; Milvus.
contrasts_with: Four LLM-agent learning paradigms the paper explicitly positions against (Figure 1): (1) Stateless Execution (standard agents that discard experience, e.g. ReAct, CoT - 'operational amnesia'); (2) Learning by Raw Trajectories (retrieving un-distilled past trajectories - mimics solutions, fails to abstract); (3) Learning via External Scribing (relying on a powerful EXTERNAL teacher LLM to distill insights, e.g. ExpeL / Memento - treats reflections as transient hints, leaves intrinsic policy unchanged); EvolveR contrasts by self-distilling its own experiences into abstract principles AND evolving its policy via RL (closed loop). Also contrasts with standard RAG/Search-R1 (fixes external-knowledge gaps but does not learn from the agent's own interaction strategy) and with SFT-on-successes (cannot leverage failures).
lineage: Group D (case-based / experience-driven planning agents): a 2025/2026 self-evolving agent that fuses experience-memory distillation (ExpeL/Reflexion lineage) with agentic search-RL (Search-R1/O2-Searcher/GRPO). It advances the experience-planner line from raw-trajectory recall (ExpeL) and external-teacher reflection (ExpeL/Memento) toward a fully self-contained closed loop that (a) self-distills its own trajectories into abstract, scored, curated strategic principles and (b) co-evolves the policy via RL on the same experience-guided trajectories - distinguishing it from both static RAG planners and memory-only experiential agents.
